statement: Recommend-and-proceed: no ritual questions, no permission-seeking for decisions derivable from context; surface the decision taken and why.
why: Owner repeatedly rejects ceremony; wants momentum with visible reasoning.
howToApply: Pick the obvious option, state it in one line, proceed; ask ONLY when the answer genuinely changes the path.

statement: Be exhaustive: cover every surface a change touches (indexes, counts, cross-refs, proof rows) — partial sweeps are worse than none.
why: Owner treats known-inconsistent state as a violation of the system's own doctrine.
howToApply: After any plan/doc change, grep for every counting/reference surface and sweep them all in one checkpoint.

statement: Orchestrator does NOT code: spawn many cheap workers (Sonnet for crates, Haiku for docs/fixtures, Opus only for doctrine authoring), coordinate, verify, integrate.
why: Token economics + the thesis that capsule discipline substitutes for model strength (L8).
howToApply: Primary lane only reads/verifies/merges/spawns; workers own all file production inside their owns: set.

statement: Commit+push a checkpoint after EVERY step — this harness has no local undo; the remote is the only save button.
why: Owner: 'unlike codex and cursor u have 0 ability to undo'.
howToApply: A step is not done until its bytes are on origin; scoped commits, one revertable point each.

statement: Never end a turn in a fragile state: all claimable work spawned + a watchdog/loop armed whenever anything is in flight; run self-driving loops until the goal, not until the next reply.
why: Owner hit the stall live: 'the session stopped! goal not yet reached'.
howToApply: Cron/wakeup chain per L14/L16; tick = mail/liveness/verify/integrate/respawn/dispatch/re-arm.

statement: Plans are workpack DIRECTORIES (capsuled, owns/deps/proof per pack), never one big markdown; workers read only their pack + routed indexes.
why: Context economy + parallel disjoint execution + provable per-pack DONE.

statement: Everything learned must LAND in a durable, preferably shipped surface (rule+fixtures, doctrine block, skill, graph node) — 'a lesson without a landed artifact is a TODO wearing a hat'.

howToApply: On any fault/insight: append ledger/memory record with routes + landedAt; fail-closed doctor (x05) enforces landing.

statement: Report memory updates back to the user as they happen: 'lesson learnt updated', 'user pref updated' — the human stays in the learning loop.

howToApply: Whenever a ledger row or memory record lands, name it (id + one-line summary) in the user-facing reply.

statement: Global over per-project: tools (MCP) register at user scope (the ~/.claude.json codebase-memory pattern); end-state is a versioned binary — 'update enforcer' = binary swap, never repo-coupled.
why: Zero-per-repo-config UX; decouple the tool from any checkout.
howToApply: Installers write user-level registries with absolute paths; transitional repo-wiring is labeled and torn out at cutover.

statement: Dogfood live while building: run the old system against the new work at micro/file scope, so every rough edge becomes benchmark + lesson data for the replacement.
why: Produces the before/after dataset proving the rewrite won (speed/stability/faults) — not vibes.
howToApply: Every worker runs ocentra_enforcer_check on its own files and reports findings verbatim-summarized; findings feed the ledger.

statement: Session/usage limits are a live orchestration constraint: throttle loop cadence, cap spawns, halt on limit-death signals, schedule past reset; ticks idempotent so queued duplicates collapse to one; workers checkpoint mid-pack so limit-death loses minutes not packs; workers self-report model (harness meta omits it).

howToApply: Loop at 15m with spawn cap 2; on session-limit in any worker result: no spawns, one wakeup past reset; started-mail must include model; mid-pack checkpoint at first proof-green.

statement: Limit-death salvage is a TRIAGE, not a blanket respawn (L38): after the shared session-limit killed dart/cfml/react lanes with 0 pushed commits, their isolated worktrees held work at 3 completeness levels. Rule: finished self-contained crate => orchestrator integrates directly (cherry-pick equivalent); partially-wired file => fresh worker ADOPTS the salvaged files from the dead worktree path and finishes wiring only; stub => discard + rebuild. New fixture extensions get EOL-pinned the same turn.
why: Owner wants everything done in one go with minimal waste; blindly respawning all 3 would have thrown away a finished dart crate, and blindly integrating all 3 would have committed an unwired react file that breaks parity.
howToApply: On any lane death, git status the worktree first; classify a/b/c; only then act. Pin new golden extensions in .gitattributes immediately (L34/L35).
